comment:
Was blessed to have had the opportunity to take professor Berryhill's Property and Environmental law classes.  He kept you thinking and was a great friend in and outside of the classroom.

A great person without question!

One of the best all-around people you will find. If you ask for help he will give as much as required. Don't let his sometimes pompous perosna get in the way - he truly wants you to learn, not regurgitate. I'd take him for anything he chooses to teach.

His sense of humour is distinct, and he carries his deep convictions into his approach.  He evaluates equally, and immersing into the material without analyzing effects of possible character differences is productive.  He cherishes the way in which he can impact his students.

Berryhill teaches at Regent for bar prep and was my private tutor for the bar. I passed the bar, first time, because of him. If *you* put in the work, he'll bend over backwards to help you succeed, but he doesn't just spoon feed his students. He's also the most approachable prof I've ever had bc he doesn't take himself so seriously.

People seem to either love him or hate him. The midterm was very fair, but the actual class discussions can be a bit challenging.  He wants you to think a certain way, which can be a struggle sometimes.  Not taking Berryhill at least once would be a mistake.

Professor Beryhill is an amazing teacher.  There is no doubt that he is a very difficult professor, but the upside is that you will receive the best education under him.  Best professor, hands down, and he really cares.  He is also very knowledgeable of pop culture and has an impeccable sense of style... unlike Devin who wears ugly shoes.

Berryhill is hard, there's no question, but you've gotta love him anyways. The man knows his contracts (and his baseball statistics) and you will as well by the end of the semester. It will take a lot of work, and you will feel stupid most of the time, but he's one of the best. Take him if you can!
He is incomprehensible, but he has some great one-liners.
Berryhill is the best!  If you missed him in Property, take him in Land Use.  There is no one in Virginia who has the knowledge and ability to instruct than W. Wade.

"Tough but fair"?! He's not a tough grader. But he's such a poor TEACHER that its tough to learn from him. Sure he's smart and will answer questions outside of class, but I'm not paying to listen to him talk about how smart he is. I want professors who TEACH. Not spoon feed, not walk around with their chest puffed out, TEACH. And he can't.

Berryhill is the classic law school professor.  Take every class from him you can.  No other professor will make sure you know the material like him.  Sure he isn't easy, learning the law isn't supposed to be easy.  But, his grades are fair and he's the most entertaining professor at UR.

Truly a great guy with a wealth of knowledge, the trouble is absorbing that knowledge.  Loves to play "hide the ball" (regardless of his insistence to the contrary) and his exams are among the most difficult I have ever taken.  That said, if you take his class YOU WILL know the subject well, BUT IT IS IN NO SENSE the easy way to learn it.

Professor Berryhill is tough but fair. You need to prepare very well to get the most from his class. He does not just handout answers he ensures that you learn the material. He is helpful and will answer your questions outside of class.

If you want to learn Property, this is the course.  If you want someone to teach you, take someone else.  Sure he's tough, but by the end of class you will know the material.  This guy is what law school is all about.

From the class of 91.  I was just thinking about Prof. Berryhill and googled him and found this page.  The thing is that most of what is said here is true, but Sitting here almost 20 years later I can say I wish I could sit in his class again and learn some more.  Yes, he is a classic "Paper Chase" professor.  It takes years to appreciate him.

His "lectures" were completely useless, 1.5 hour rant sessions of the "I'm brilliant/You're stupid" variety. The best thing to do is to be as inactive in class as possible, hit the hornbooks, study guides and caselaw, and study only for the exam. Aside from Bar Review, you won't hear one piece of useful information come from his mouth to your ears.

The comments here separate the wheat from the chaff.  People who come to law school and expect to be taught will do poorly.  People who come to learn do well.  Berryhill is a law professor in the Paper Chase mold, and excels at it.
He's a puppetmaster... in a good way.  He challenges his students to find the best in them.
The quintessential law school experience

This is the best damn law professor in the state.  idf you want to pass the bar or even learn the law, this is the man who can prepare you.  If  you want to sit on your ass and read the outline your best friend's cousin did at W&M, dont waste your time. Success follows hard work.  THANKS BERRYHILL -

For whatever reason, he has been permitted (by the powers that be) to belittle and ridicule his students for years. The explanation:  He has tenure.  Not a good enough reason, but reason enough NOT to attend this law school.  This is unacceptable behavior for a lawyer, let alone an educator.  In his own words: "Get a life, stuuupid!"

A "classic" law professor. Be prepared for class, don't expect him to give you the answers. I studied and kept up on the material and I did well. Don't be intimidated by his in class demeanor. Talk to him outside of class and you'll see he's a really nice guy.

Definately does not spell ANYTHING out for you. But keeps you slightly terrified and entertained. Expect to learn most of it on your own and to use him as motivation to study rather than a means to learn. In the end he makes you think, which is different from learning a subject. Instead youget a lot of mental exercise and interesting words o wisdom

By far the best class I had in law school. It's not socratic, so you get to know the "real" Berryhill. He was always helpful and insightful - and he definitely made you think. He was willing to help on the papers, and he treats his students very well, even after they are out of his class.

Wade is great.  He does play hide-the-ball, so he's not always clear, but he forces you to figure the material out.  He's entertaining and always willing to talk or answer questions.  He is an integral part of the law school experience.

HATED this class. Berryhill has followers for some unknown reason, but pay them no mind. Hes full of himself and mean as a snake. His sense of humor is, admittedly, terrific. But that doesn't excuse the rest of it. Just get through it and avoid him for the
VERY full of himself, and he shouldn't be, because he's a horrible teacher.
A for entertainment.  F for instruction.  You are better off taking someone else if you are actually interested in the subject.
Superb. I felt frustrated and confused at various points in the class, but his methods work.  By the end of the class I knew the material cold. Take him if you can.
Prof Berryhill's environmental seminars are outstanding.  If that is your interest, take as many of his seminars as you can.

Great instructor, but has a "different" personality. Focuses on truly understanding the material versus rote memorization. I got a kick out of him, others did not. In my opinion he was one of the best first year professors.

If you plan to sit for the Virginia Bar, take his bar review course.  All comments above regarding law school classroom observations notwithstanding, this professor runs THE bar prep course in the Commonwealth!

once you understand his goal is to teach you how to learn rather than to spoon feed you the material he makes a lot more sense. as a first year class property is very hard but what he has to offer can make the rest of law school easier

If i were rating on entertainment Berry would rate high. But Im not, his rating is based on teaching ability and he sucks. Maybe if he spent less time preening and trying to confuse and more time explaining the concepts people would have a clue what the hell is going on.
do not take Berryhill if you can help it!  Definitely one of the worst profs I have ever had.
come prepared

He is a bad professor.  He may have been there for a long time, but he's stunningly in love with himself to the detriment of his effectiveness as a professor.  Very unclear in class, more 'ranting' than teaching, and you will leave this course more confused and knowing less than you did before it.
Class is somewhat interesting, but was very put off by Mr. Berryhill's belief that he is a.) God's gift to teaching law b.) God's other gift to once praticing law.
No Comments
do not go to class unprepared
